attempts.explanation:
## What this letter says
You had a painful right knee. You had a knee replacement many years ago. The pain and soreness slowly got worse.
An X-ray showed the plastic part (poly) seems to be very worn out.
You had an operation called a poly exchange of the right total knee.
You are stable now. You did well. You walked with little help during physical therapy (PT). Your pain pills by mouth worked well.
Anesthesia took out the nerve block in your leg (femoral nerve block).
Your INR was 1.9 when you left. INR is a blood test.
You are going home with your son. He will help and look after you.

## What you need to do
1. Eat your regular diet.
2. Put weight on your right leg as much as you can manage.
3. Keep doing your physical therapy exercises.
4. Have lab checks twice a week. They check your INR while you take Coumadin.
5. See Dr. ABC in two weeks.
6. Go home to the care of your son.
7. Call the office or go back to the emergency room if you have any concerns. See the last section.

## Dates and medicines
- Follow up with Dr. ABC: in two weeks. The letter does not give the exact date.
- Coumadin: 4 milligrams a day.
- Vicodin 5/500 milligrams: take one to two tablets by mouth every 4 to 6 hours.
- Home medicines: the letter says to resume them. It does not name them.

## Questions to ask your doctor
1. What is the exact date of my visit with Dr. ABC?
2. Which home medicines should I take again?
3. Were Coumadin and Vicodin new for me, or ones I took before?

## When to get urgent help
Call the office or go back to the emergency room for any concerns. This includes:
- more redness
- swelling
- drainage
- fever
- any concern about the operation or the cut (incision) site
